reasoning_content:
Let me check the actual repository on GitLab to see if these files exist there. The repo at gitlab.opencode.de. Let me check via git whether the origin has these files. Actually the checkout is at HEAD 7edb795 which is origin/main. Let me check whether the files exist upstream currently.

Actually - wait. Maybe these components are actually expected to be excluded but the app still works because they're not used at runtime? No, Vite fails to build. And in dev mode Vite would also fail when loading NavUser.

Hmm, but the guide says npm run dev, not build. In dev mode, Vite compiles on demand. NavUser is imported by AppSidebar which is imported by AppSidebarLayout. But is AppSidebarLayout actually used by MainPage? MainPage doesn't use a layout. Let me check MainController and whether the page uses AppLayout.

Let me look at the whole MainPage.vue template.

Actually, in dev mode, Vite only resolves modules that are actually imported in the dependency graph of the loaded page. If MainPage doesn't import AppSidebar → NavUser, then it's never loaded. Let me check.

MainPage imports Navigation, Sensor, Ochsi, HomeInfoCard, SensorCard. No layout. So NavUser is not part of the graph for the home page. So dev mode might work fine!

But the production build (npm run build) processes ALL modules including via glob of pages/**/*.vue and the ssr entry. Actually the build input is only resources/js/app.ts and ssr.ts. app.ts uses import.meta.glob('./pages/**/*.vue') which includes all pages. Dashboard.vue uses AppLayout. Let me check AppLayout.

So build includes Dashboard → AppLayout → AppSidebarLayout → AppSidebar → NavUser → UserMenuContent (missing). Hence build fails.

But is that part of the required installation? The guide's local dev setup uses `composer dev` (php artisan serve + npm run dev). The production deployment uses `npm run build`. 

The task is to install the software. Following the local dev setup. But we should verify the app works. Let me consider: maybe the intended install just needs composer dev to run. But the missing file is a genuine repo defect.

However, maybe the missing files are actually present in the upstream repo and the checkout somehow lost them. Let me check the upstream remote for the file.
